title: Resolved crew offers block later crews for the same members and activity forever

The crewNotFormed text says 'I'll keep you in mind for the next plan'. The same code is on claude/formal-main.
proposal: Trigger: yoga plan P1, a, b and c say 'again', so an offer goes out. b says no and c is silent, so the offer times out as crew_not_formed. Weeks later at yoga plan P2, a, c, d and e all say 'again'. positive minus inCrew{a,b,c} = {d,e}, which is under 3, so no offer goes out ever. Fix: pass this.crews plus only the offers that are not resolved. Model: add a second offer and activity to plan_crew.qnt (G1) and add a witness that a new positive group gets an offer.

title: A formed crew that falls under 3 seat-ok members, or that holds a blocked pair, never ends
detail: The only exit in crewSessions is 3 'done' sessions. (a) A member stops, goes on watch, becomes a minor or is deleted. Then members.length < minMembers, so the loop does `continue` every day forever. The crew got 'Your weekly crew is on', no member hears that it stopped, and the members stay in inCrew (see the defect above). (b) a blocks b inside crew a,b,c,d. planSeatOk has no pair check, so each week a session is proposed with both. The human reviewer approves, and approvalCheck returns blocked_pair and closes the item. 'done' never reaches 3, so the crew loops weekly for ever. This is what is left of SD-211 (refuted only because approval stops the probe).
proposal: Trigger (b): crew of 4 formed. a texts 'block b'. Run 3 weeks with review auto: 3 review_invalidated blocked_pair, 0 done, no handoff, and the loop goes on. Fix: in crewSessions, drop a blocked pair (or end the crew), and end the crew (handedOff or a new ended state) when seat-ok members stay under minMembers. Add an integration case with mini.ts, and add the liveness property G3 to the model.

title: sessionSlotOnce cannot fail: it restates the crewTick guard
detail: planId = slot and not(dup) is a guard of crewTick, so the invariant holds by construction. SD-144's mechanism (the dedupe looked up plan ids in the map of opportunity ids) cannot be expressed in the model. The pass is vacuous for the regression it is said to guard.
proposal: Model the plan id as a function of (crew, start computed from now with minLead), and the opportunity id as a separate counter. Do the dedupe on the plan id. Then the invariant compares (crew, start) pairs across all session opportunities, not crewSessions entries.

title: handoffCountsSessions counts sessions that did not fail, not sessions that were held; crewOptedIn's size bound holds only because nothing removes members
detail: The rule is 3 sessions that took place ('done'). The invariant accepts 'review' as well and is saved only by the guard. crewOptedIn requires crewMembers.size >= 3 at all times, but the code shrinks crew.members on forget, so this is a statement about formation that the model checks forever only because deletion is not modelled.
proposal: Use the count of held sessions >= HANDOFF. State crewOptedIn on a formation snapshot so that adding forget (G4) does not break it falsely.

title: The seatOk comment says busyOk, but crewSessions calls planSeatOk without it; the header anchors are stale
detail: crewSessions uses planSeatOk(m) with no options, so a member busy in another open opportunity is left out of that session (and can drop the seats under 3 for that week). seatOk also leaves out stage active, onlyWhenAsked, account and validAge. The anchors crewCheck 3212, onCrewAnswer 3242, resolveCrew 3252 and crewSessions 3270 are now 3377, 3407, 3417 and 3435.
proposal: Add a transient `busy` actor set that the session seat filter reads, and that the resolve filter (formal-main) does not read. Update the anchors.

title: No offer creation: crewCheck, detectCrews, the late join and the send gates are absent
detail: init starts at 'offered' with fixed CREW0. Missing: the inCrew rule and the `existing` list (the never-pruned-offers defect), the late-join path that grows offered after some answers (the two-crews defect), per-recipient refusals (cap, opt-out, hold, leak guard), where a refused offer leaves an offered member who can never answer, and the plansOn gate. Adding these breaks a one-crew-per-activity invariant and a 'positive group gets an offer' witness.
proposal: Extend plan_crew.qnt with a crewOffer(plan, positives) action over 2 activities and 4 to 5 members, an offered set that can grow, and a refused-send event. Add oneCrewPerActivity, and a witness that a second positive group is offered.

title: No blocks and no approval invalidation, so the planned crewRechecksBlocks invariant is missing from both models
detail: Section 6.7 planned crewRechecksBlocks. SD-211 was refuted because approvalCheck catches the blocked pair. Neither plan_run.qnt nor plan_crew.qnt models a block between crew members, so the weekly invalidation loop (the dead-crew defect, part b) is not visible.
proposal: Add a block(a,b) actor event. Add the session end 'invalidated' when a blocked pair is present at approval. Invariant: no session proposal holds a blocked pair (it fails today). Liveness: the crew ends.

title: No end state other than handoff, and no liveness property
detail: Probe: the invariant crewNotDead (formed and not handed off implies >= 3 seat-ok members) is violated in 5 steps (formed, then watch(c)). Nothing in safety, the witnesses or the run tests marks a crew that can never run again.
proposal: Add crewStage 'ended' (or a temporal property formed ~> handedOff or ended under fairness on crewTick), and a witness_deadCrew. Keep it in skippedDefects until the code fix lands.

title: No member deletion (forget)
detail: forget deletes every opportunity that has the member, including done crew sessions, so the 'done' count drops and the handoff comes later. It also removes the member from crews and offers, so a crew can go under 3 members. Adding this action breaks crewOptedIn as written (see the model error above).
proposal: Add forget(m): remove m from crewMembers, crewYes and crewNo, and delete the sessions that m was invited to. Check that handoff still counts correctly and that the crew ends (liveness).

title: Session slot is decoupled from the clock; daily cadence and the plansOn gate are absent
detail: crewWeekPass moves freely while `now` moves separately. In the code, start is computed from now (minLead 72h, cadence 7d), and crewSessions runs once a day after the planner, only when plans and matchingEnabled are on. When matching is off, offers never time out, but onCrewAnswer still forms crews (crewFormed is sent) and no session runs.
proposal: Derive the slot from now (slot = first k with start_k >= now+lead), and add a matchingEnabled actor flag that disables crewTimeout and crewTick but not crewAnswer.

title: The session lifecycle is collapsed to review -> held or failed
detail: Missing: probing and scheduled (OPEN_STAGES), invalidation at approval (busy_elsewhere, on_watch, blocked_pair), reject -> markDeclined for every crew pair, withReach outsiders who get the plain plan probe, and handleDrop under quorum. In the code, 'done' means scheduled with meeting+3h passed, even when nobody came. These do not break the current invariants, but they are needed for the block and liveness checks.
proposal: Add session ends 'invalidated' and 'rejected' (with markDeclined of pairs), and an outsider seat, when G2 and G3 are added.

title: The awaiting slot is not modelled; crewAnswer is always delivered
detail: In the code, a crew answer counts only while awaiting=crew. awaiting is cleared after 3 days and overwritten by check-in, feedback or growth asks. A member who joins late can answer after the resolve. Adding the slot shows the lost-answer defect and makes crew_not_formed reachable more often.
proposal: Add an awaiting map with an overwrite event (other ask) and a 3-day clear. Add a witness: a member's yes after the resolve gets no reply.

title: SD-444 notice part (crewEndHeard) is still skipped

title: submitProfile 'accepted' can never be false; not_member path missing
detail: accepted = not(banned(now)) but bearerOk already refuses that ban, so the branch is dead. The service answers not_member for a missing runtime member, a non-active state or a number ban, after the quota was counted.

title: leave(listenerFails) and declineUnder13 are cleaner and stronger than the code
detail: A failed leave in code has already forgotten the network member and photos. declineUnder13 models only service statedAge (forgetPhone, every app) and needs a membership; the accounts.declineUnderAge path forgets only joined apps and nothing for a null person, so grantDiesWithPerson passes vacuously for that path.

title: Stale guards fixed only in the formal-main model
detail: exchReplay requires an unexpired code (code checks usedAt first, handler.ts:593-599); approveRead is disabled instead of deleting the request (handler.ts:516-522); prepareSignup refuses 13-17 and has stillTheirs as a guard instead of revoking (tools.ts:286-289).

title: requestRetention is stronger than the code's sweep timing
detail: The model deletes a request exactly at TTL. The code deletes it at the next sweep (60 s guard, only after a tick on this instance, errors swallowed), so the README 10-minute bound is exceeded by up to one sweep period or more.
proposal: Model the sweep as a separate action that may lag, with the invariant stated as TTL plus one sweep period, or document the overshoot in the README.

title: Model ignores the ban exception in onForget (8e96df9); three photo rules fail when the model follows the code
detail: Code deletes a person's photos on leave and on delete everything only when personBanned is false. The model's leaveHide and delHide always hide every row. In a scratch copy with the code's ban guard, noPhotoAfterForget is violated in 195 ms (upload, show, banCommit, banDrop, banRestrict, leaveConsent, leaveNetForget, leaveHideBanned, leaveEnd, leaveForgetMembership). noPhotoForForgottenMember and the not-deleted half of photoOnlyForAdult fail the same way. This is the open item from the drift review on claude/formal-main.
proposal: Add the banned guard to leaveHide and delHide. Restate the three rules as 'unless banned when the forget ran' with a bannedAtForget ghost. Add banKeepsPhotos (the identity_sagas rule) to this model.

title: SD-017 is fixed in code (709be0b), but the model still does a whole-row write and keeps banSticks out of safety
detail: consentAnswer now calls updateMembership(person, slop, [who.m.state], {profile}). This is a compare-and-set that never writes the state. consentYesWrite still sets membership: caSnap. The findings file says 'not fixed on this branch'. The commit is an ancestor of the model commit 5b22040.
proposal: Make consentYesWrite write only when membership == caSnap and never write the state. Move banSticks into safety and change sd017ConsentWriteUndoesBanTest so that it expects the ban to stick.

title: The ban retry for an unfinished ban (e361184) is not modelled, so the ratingLeft carve-out for SD-005 is permanent
detail: banCommit needs not(st.banned). The code lets staff run the ban again when banUnfinished is true (a live membership or an unrestricted member), and the retry calls dropRatings. After a crash between the ban rows and dropRatings, the model has no way to finish, so ratingLeft leaves out the ban rating for good.
proposal: Add a banRetry action, enabled when banned and the membership is LIVE, that runs banDrop and banRestrict again. Limit ratingLeft for the ban to 'until a staff retry', or state the rule as eventually true after a retry.

title: Checking rules only after one purge pass hides the crash-to-purge window, and matchRead is not the engine's gate
detail: Every state rule is checked on purged(st). The code runs rt.tick() (matching) before svc.purge(), so a residue that the purge would clear can be used in that tick. matchRead is gated on LIVE membership, netMember and not banned. The engine instead uses canRatePhotos on the member age and verify:age:fail. usedInMatching is only a witness, and no rule reads it.
proposal: Give matchRead the engine guard (netAge >= 18 and not ageFail). Add a rule, checked in every state, that a rating is used in matching only for an adult member. Model the tick-before-purge order after a crash.

title: The probe passes a held flag the code never passes, and the lowest age instead of the member age
detail: The code calls probePhotoRefs({age, photoConsent: SLOP_PROBE_PHOTOS, photoIds: []}, ...) with no held flag, and age is the member age from the snapshot. The model passes held = banned or not LIVE and uses st.age (the lowest age). The check is vacuous today because photoIds is empty. Once ids are wired, the model would hide a missing held check and a stale member age. The probe guard st.rating is not in the code.
proposal: Use held = false and netAge in probe, and remove the st.rating guard (keep it only as a focus weight).

title: ageCommit models the hook only on a drop, but the code reruns onAgeLowered on every recordAge

So when the person states an age again, the Q-1 and Q-2 residues are repaired. The model has no such action, so it understates recovery. Adding the action cannot break a rule.
proposal: Add an ageRestate action that runs the full age hook when age < 18.

detail: Proof entries are keyed by the open SQL transaction, so the Cloud calls must run under the locks. The feature is off in production (NETWORK_PROFILE_REVIEW_ENABLED). title: SD-172 cutoff invariants: fixable without a wire change

title: Number change (PRD F25, startNumberChange, confirmNumberChange, movePhone) is not modelled
detail: No action moves a person to another number. Adding the move breaks staleSessionNoAct today (D1, probe). The confirm race with an OTP login on the new number is harmless, because only the holder of that number can log in.

title: Only one open app with a correct consent wording, and textJoin is always an adult
where: quint/auth_edge.qnt:519-559,572-589 (HEAD); fm decisions.ts:134-146; service.ts statedAge path
detail: The invite_only and consent_wording exits and the member 'existing' step with a lower age cannot be reached, so under13NothingStored cannot see D4. The text under-13 path never writes under13At, and it leaves earlier person-less web sessions of the number in place.

title: The account ops stop, share, revokeShare, home, resume and GET /api/me are not in op
detail: Each of these uses personFor(who.e164). home and /me also accept a person-less session (api.ts:515,533). With G1 or G2 each one is a foreign act. stop is the worst case: it opts another person out on every app.
proposal: Add 'stop' (it writes the opt-out) and 'me' (it reads firstName) to op, and record them in foreignActs.

title: Cookies in flight, the 60 s grace token and logout are not modelled
detail: The model's account action always uses the jar head. Old tokens that still work in their grace time, logout, and which cookie a browser keeps after a fork are absent. This hides D5.
proposal: Give each request the token it carries (from the jar, or an older one in its grace time), and add logout. Add an availability witness: no live head is revoked by the actor's own join.

title: The 12-month hold, held paths and clearHold are not modelled
detail: seen() puts a number on hold at login, verify then makes a person-null session, export and delete refuse a held number, and clearHold same_owner neither binds nor revokes the person-null sessions made during the hold. I expect no invariant to break, because only the holder can log in during a hold.

title: banNumber needs a person; staff can ban a number with no person
detail: Bans by phone hash exist without a person (for example banUnfinished). OTP start and verify check by hash. Adding these bans should keep safety, and it covers the ban and OTP interleavings for person-less numbers.
proposal: Drop the personFor != NONE precondition from banNumber.

title: Multi-app scope of challenges, sessions and bindSessions
detail: Challenges are per (app, number) and sessions are per app, but bindSessions and forgetPersonlessSessions span every app of the number. A join on one site revokes the same human's person-less session on another site. This is harmless (a re-login), but the model cannot show it.
proposal: Add a second open app id to sessions and challenges, behind a small bound.

title: Cloud: the non-production validation cache and the staging-local per-app mode are not modelled
detail: In non-production Cloud mode a positive validation is reused for 60 s, so a revoked delegation can act for up to 60 s. In staging-local, cloudFor(app) covers one app only, so the other apps use OTP. oneAuthMode is global and unavailableNoAccess assumes there is no cache. This applies to dev and staging only.
proposal: Say in the header that production-v1 is the only mode modelled, or add a cache-TTL action for staging.

title: cloudGrantAuthority and validateCloudGrant (Cloud MCP grants) are not modelled
detail: A grant with personId null is valid whoever owns the number now. This is the person-less pattern of SD-054, on MCP grants.
proposal: Hand to oauth_mcp: check grantStillTheirs and the null-personId grant after a number gets a person or a move.

title: cloudLogin assumes that the Cloud phone proof names the number's current holder
detail: Cloud signs the account's 'matching verified phone projection', verified at some earlier time, not a code sent now. If a Cloud account keeps a recycled number, the earlier holder signs in on the web and gets the new holder's person. This assumption is not listed in the header's abstractions.

detail: A ban that commits between the ban check and sessions.create gives a session for a banned number. This is harmless in the code: /me, export and join refuse a banned number. But the model's claim that 'the awaits change nothing an invariant reads' is false.

title: The staleSessionNoAct carve-out allows an earlier holder's chain to create a person and an opt-in
detail: The 'chain whose own web join created it' exception is checked by chain, not by holder. probeEarlierHolderJoinTest passes with safety while bob opts in alice's phone (D3).

title: under13NothingStored is vacuous outside the open-app web join

proposal: Fix now: restore 'ageLoweredByOther or lowered' in the under-age branch, then rerun quint:check. It should pass until G2 is added, and then fail on D2 until D2 is fixed.

title: SD-107: a suppressed number cannot sign in through Cloud (skipped, founder decision)
detail: Since the 2026-10-19 correction there is no web rejoin. But if the agent signup's phone-confirm link is the Cloud sign-in, a number that deleted everything can rejoin only by text.
proposal: This cannot be fixed without a founder decision. Ask whether the agent signup confirm link uses Cloud. Keep the witness.

title: SD-308: the other proof parsers still allow no clock skew
detail: proofWindowOk refuses issuedAt > now for the proofs that Cloud issues. SD-181 fixed only the login delegation. This is in scope and small.
proposal: Add a skew argument (30 s, for issuedAt only) to proofWindowOk for Cloud-issued proofs, with one integration case per endpoint. Model it in profile_learning or in a small proof-window module.

title: SD-180 is accepted as harmless for safety, but it causes a logout after a join
detail: The two-head fork and the grace token, together with bindSessions, revoke the head that the browser keeps (D5).
proposal: Track this as D5. Add an availability witness after G5.

title: The carrier-aging assumption (45 days) is a precondition that the code does not enforce
detail: Only this assumption keeps an old holder's OTP code, and with D3's fix the old session, away from a new holder. Some VoIP providers recycle numbers faster.
proposal: With D3's fix, write the cap next to the assumption. A person-less chain must be shorter than the shortest aging assumed. Keep carrierReassign's precondition and document the VoIP exception.

title: Most safety conjuncts are ghost flags that only restate their action's own guard
detail: 17 of the 21 conjuncts in safety use a flag that an action sets from a condition its own guard already rules out, so the conjunct cannot fail. The affected values are minorNeverCandidate, heldNeverCandidate, locatedBeforeMatch, budgetAcrossAssign, engineAgreesWithGate, judgeCacheReused, activityFitsSlot, askTerminates, answersReachLoop, engineNeverSelectsHeld, declineScopedToJob, confirmedInOwnThread, filledRecorded, closedTerminal, openingsPreserved and acceptedPostingPersists. For example, gateOk requires netMemberOk, and netMemberOk already means adult and not held. These values record that each fix happened. They cannot catch a bug that comes from two actions interacting.
proposal: Replace each ghost flag with a state predicate over opp, billed or posting that does not repeat the guard. Turn the engine into an adversary: slopDailyRun picks any pair allowed by engine rules written from rules.ts and filters.ts on their own, and the Network gate becomes the thing under test.

title: No approval-time recheck and no dropMember: in the model a minor or held member is still probed after review
detail: In the code, reviewBlock and approvalCheck refuse approval for a member who is a minor, held, opted out or busy, and dropMember closes review items when a minor signal, hold or STOP arrives. The model's slopReview approves with no checks. Probe run minorAfterReviewTest in wave3/probe/me.qnt runs daily run (a,b), then statesMinorAge(b), then approve: b gets a probe and safety stays true. The code is correct; the model leaves out the property that matters.
proposal: Add approvalCheck to slopReview(approve), and add dropMember-style closes to statesMinorAge and setHold (close in review, replaceOrClose in probing). Add state invariants noMinorProbed and noHeldProbed that check probing and scheduled opps.

title: Items closed without a reject or expiry decision still count against the engine although nobody was contacted
detail: The unsent list includes only items with review.decision 'reject' or 'expired', or review.invalidated. Several other paths close an item from review without setting a decision: reroll with no alternate (every slop item has no alternates), dropMember for a hold or STOP, callOffPair on a block, and endSeat. A probe that never went out (PROBE_WAIT expiry, or the member is away) is also left out. close() records no interaction for a close from review. So the item stays in recentProposals for 30 days, counts against each member's 2-per-7-days budget, and keeps the pair in activePairs for 7 days. This is the SD-210/SD-262 harm on paths that fix 3c059f6 did not cover.
proposal: Trigger: the daily run proposes (a,b), and staff choose 'reroll' (accepted at service.ts:142). There is no alternate, so the item closes. At the next run a and b are each billed one proposal and the pair is active-blocked. The same happens when b sends STOP while the item waits for review. Fix: build unsent from o.contacted.size === 0. Add integration cases next to engine-unsent.integration.test.ts. In the model, add a reroll action and a hold-during-review close, and widen unsentNotBilled.

title: A staff posting save can reopen a posting that was closed after it was read (TOCTOU)
detail: POST /postings reads stored(id) and checks the closed status in its own transaction, outside the network unit. It then builds status 'active' and calls applyPosting in a later unit. applyPosting never re-reads the stored status, and savePosting upserts with status = excluded.status. The SD-114 fix (ce667b2) only covers the sequential order. The model's staffSave is atomic, which assumes more than the code gives. Peon runs locally only, so this is lower order in practice.

Before the staff unit gets the network lock (for example while a daily run with the judge holds it), the manager's 'close my data analyst post' + 'yes' unit commits and endSeat runs. The staff unit then writes p back as active. Fix: re-read the stored posting inside the unit (storedPosting in applyPosting) and refuse with posting_closed. In the model, split staffSave into read and commit actions with other actions allowed between them.

title: seatCapacity is vacuous: there is one candidate, and openings never reach 0
detail: With a single candidate, a seat can never be booked past its openings. storedOpenings returns 1 for a closed posting, and booked items survive the close. The invariant therefore cannot show D5 or any capacity race.

title: Onboarding per-question caps, the skip list, the late-read guard and the soft questions are not modelled (open drift)
detail: These are the three open items from the formal-main drift review. The code caps every question at 2 asks and skips the question that was just answered. A late text is read only when it adds a new tag or moves the next reason. The soft questions and the slop_zip / slop_seeks / slop_gender split also exist. The founder default (seeks set to straight after two seeks asks) makes members matchable on an inferred seeks, and the model's 'core' bit cannot express that. Adding the caps makes noBasicsAfterAnswer reachable on more paths, and it exposes the location lockout (finding 6).
proposal: Add askCounts per reason to Ob, use skip in nextMsg, apply the drift's late guard, and add a seeksDefaulted bit.

title: Probe expiry, never-sent probes, the away refusal and reroll are missing from the slop probe lifecycle
detail: The model's probing ends only with a yes or a no. The code also has PROBE_TTL (26 h) silence, PROBE_WAIT (the probe never sent), the away refusal, time retry, no common time and replaceOrClose. Each of these closes as 'expired', which gives a 7-day engine re-probe and no 60-day decline. A reroll closes the item and runs markDeclined. These paths are where D1 lives.
proposal: Add slopExpire(p, contacted: bool) and slopReroll(p). Widen unsentNotBilled to 'no contacted member implies not billed'.

title: Location is a single bit; the zip and area tags, the unknown-zip state and the anchor fallback are not modelled
detail: The model cannot express D2 (a stale area tag) or the slop_zip and slop_location fallbacks for each tag. Adding this would make a generalised deletedFieldClearsTag fail on the current code.
proposal: Replace loc with {zip: none|known|unknown, area: bool} and model the replaces lists from extract.ts:921-924.

title: Peon draft lifecycle, staff create and re-close, and the verifyEmployer race are missing
detail: In the code, the 3-day sweep clears awaiting 'posting', and expect() replaces it with a probe, so the draft is lost. Incomplete drafts are dropped after 2 asks. There is also the 'which post?' step. Staff can create a new posting with no id, and staff can close an already closed posting, which rewrites closedReason (filled to closed). verifyEmployer checks managerProblem and writes in separate transactions. None of this breaks safety, because the model is a superset for drafts. The re-close path is not checked by filledRecorded.
proposal: Add draft expiry, staffCreate and staffClose on a closed posting. Add an invariant that closedReason 'filled' is never overwritten.

title: Daily-run framing and engine ask scheduling are missing
detail: The code runs once per NY day in the run hour, honours the matchingEnabled switch and the maxNewPerDay daily_cap, and runs player proposals first. slopAssign can select one member twice in a run through backup rounds. sendAsks runs only for stage 'active', with no awaiting, every ASK_EVERY_DAYS (7). The engine's own hard-field asks are weekly and capped at maxAsksPerField 2, and there are also slop_type and slop_widen. These narrow the model. They are needed for liveness witnesses and for the location lockout.
proposal: Add lastRunDay, maxNewPerDay and a matchingEnabled bit. Add an engineHardAsk(m, field) action with the cap and the 7-day interval.

title: Engine-only slop holds, booked-date backout, no-show and metRecently are not modelled
detail: Missing: review_hold (verification, safety cues, trust_review from noShows, negativeFrom, blockedBy or eagerYes), recently_matched pacing, basics_pending, the romanceGate verified-adult check, handleDrop and cancel, check-in outcomes, and metRecently in the gate. Only metRecently could break an invariant (D4, peon). The rest only remove pairs.
proposal: Add a met-or-no-show interaction per pair with metRecently in the gate, keyed the way the code keys it (manager id, not seat). This exposes D4.

title: The judge cache lives in process memory: it is lost at restart, not shared across replicas, and invalidated by profile revision
detail: judgeCache is a private field. importState and exportState do not carry it, so a restart or a second replica repeats every judge call. judgeCacheReused would fail if a restart action were added. This is a cost issue only, since the judge is off by default (NETWORK_ENGINE_JUDGE).
proposal: Add a restart action that clears judgeLast. Keep the invariant for in-process runs, or persist the cache.

title: Plan machines attention-compose and slop-member-history are not in the model; ProbeFlow parallel and group modes are left out
detail: Section 6.16 lists 15 machines, but the model header names 13. History feeds trust_review holds and peon history (SD-441). For ProbeFlow, the parallel and group-quorum modes and answer overwrites are missing. Checked by hand: every mode ends once everyone has answered.
proposal: Name the two missing machines as left out (with a reason) in the header and in the findings. If history is added, model it as counters feeding a hold.

title: The flow part checks the unwired ProbeFlow library, and planSeatHonorsHoldout is a tautology of the model's own function
detail: startProbeFlow and recordProbeAnswer have no caller outside attention.ts; production consent runs on the Network's Opp stages. planReason is a pure def inside the model, and the invariant checks that def against nondeterministic facts. It reads nothing from plans.ts or filters.ts and leaves out holds, paused, category opt-out and the host/guest forgive sets.
proposal: Mark the flow part 'library only, unwired'. Either drop the plan part (plan_run.qnt owns plans) or model memberReason's rule list and forgive sets as data.

title: slopReview approve always counts a send for the first member
detail: In the code, the first probe can be refused when it is due (quiet hours, away, budget) and expire unsent after PROBE_WAIT. The model's sentTimes over-counts these, and it hides the never-sent billing case in D1.
proposal: Make the send nondeterministic: sent or held. Only a sent probe appends to sentTimes and to contacted.

title: Location answered without a location leaves the member locked out of matching (findings section 6)
detail: When the location ask is answered with something that is not a location, answeredAny is true, so the ask is never treated as silent. Both the engine and the loop cap the ask at 2. needs_location then holds forever and nothing asks again. The model shows this state, but no test has run it against the code.
proposal: In scope as a bug fix once an integration case reproduces it: treat an answered slop_location ask that left no location as silent after 7 days, or re-allow the ask after the cap at a long interval.

title: noBasicsAfterAnswer (SD-419 residual): a member who says 'no dealbreakers' is asked for basics up to two more times
detail: needsBasics reads tags only, and 'no dealbreakers' leaves no tag. The fix bounded the ask but did not remove it.
proposal: Fixable now: let needsBasics count an answered slop_basics ask (recentAsks answeredAt) as answered. Add an integration case, then move noBasicsAfterAnswer into safety.

title: A booked reveal takes the answer slot of a pending probe, so a 'no' to the probe cancels the booked plan

When the first plan then books, the reveal's onSent calls expect(booked) and replaces the probe slot. The member's answer to the second probe goes to the booked branch: 'no' runs handleDrop on the plan they wanted, and 'yes' confirms it ('Great, see you there.'). The second probe expires as a silent no after 26 h. This is not SD-043/D5: D5 covers the writers that skip expect() and says only a manager can reach this state. Here expect() itself allows the overwrite, and every plan yes-sayer can reach it.

Fix: expect() never replaces a pending probe with booked, or a member with a pending probe is left out at bookPlan. Integration test with two plans. Model: add the per-member awaiting slot and routing (G2).

Fix: rebuild the reveal text and about at flush time, or drop and note pending reveals in handleDrop. Model: G1 (a deferred reveal with the stored about).

Line safety, the unanswered-cap hold and queue-level quiet hours make rows wait for days. With the 2-day window, this can admit a row the desk took back.
proposal: Add a park and leakRelease pair of actions, plus a time-to-wait for queued rows. Keep the lost ghost per send attempt.

title: waitingSwapAsked misses a swap question that ended in the queue
detail: The swap is pushed when the question is queued. If the queue later ends the ':ask' row unsent, the swap still waits, and A was told 'I'll share your number as soon as they say'. The invariant checks only a refusal inside the unit.
proposal: Make the invariant read the ask row's status. Fix in the code: the endpoint sync drops swaps whose ask row is NOT_SENT.

title: numberMovesOnlyIfBothConsented reads 'the peer ever asked', not consent for this swap within the TTL
detail: g.consent.asked stays true for ever after any request, so a share that rests on an expired swap would pass this invariant. The rule is weaker than founder decision 9's per-item consent.
proposal: Record the swap id and the consent time in the Send, and check that the peer's consent belongs to this swap and is within the TTL at decision time.

title: Several actors and paths are not in the model; none was found to break an invariant
detail: Not modelled: trust 'watch' refusals; the duplicate-text rule; the severeBlock staff case (SD-254 fix fa81646); a missing contactOf; the swap where their share passes and mine is held, which consumes B's swap with no log row; the 'none' and photo-unavailable branches; action_limit and action_conflict; and a failed save that leaves the in-memory Network mutated. The queue's in-memory checks read that mutated state, but the admission reads Postgres.
proposal: Optional: add a severeBlock-opens-case invariant, and a 'their swap consumed' ghost for the asymmetric decision.

title: HELP from a member never gets an answer after its unit committed and its claim was lost (turn_failed loop)

title: A live but stuck compliance turn (e.g. a non-member START waiting on the join lock) blocks the sender's STOP until the gateway gives up
detail: The lease is renewed by a 30 s timer, whether or not the run makes progress, and a signed run has no deadline. A compliance claim waits for any processing compliance row of the sender. A non-member START commits its opt-in, then enters people.withLock (a process-wide promise chain plus a blocking pg_advisory_lock). If that wait hangs, the START row stays processing with a fresh lease. Every STOP retry gets turn_busy, and the STOP never reaches the ledger before the gateway stops retrying. The START opt-in stays the newest event. The scratch run test probeHungStartBlocksStop shows this (60x21 ticks, safety holds) because stopNeverLost only checks final STOPs.
proposal: Trigger: STOP earlier; non-member sends START (claims the compliance slot, writes the opt-in, blocks in withLock or unitOfWork); the person sends STOP and gets turn_busy on every retry; the gateway gives up; no STOP event. Fix options: stop renewing after a run deadline so the sweep frees the slot; or let a STOP take the slot from a non-STOP compliance turn; or write the STOP event (idempotent per ref) in the claim transaction when the slot is busy. Integration test with a blocked START promise. Model: add gwGiveUp and check stopNeverLost at give-up.

title: stopNeverLost is vacuous for a STOP that never gets a final answer; gateway give-up is not modelled

detail: The invariant only covers STOPs that are final at the gateway. title: No invariant protects leave (or START) consent; leaveNeverLost fails on HEAD and via the legacy drain on formal-main

On the formal-main model, run test probeLegacyLeaveDropped fails it: inbox.ts keeps only isStopText rows pending after 5 failed attempts, so a legacy 'leave slop' that fails 5 times is marked 'failed' and the per-app opt-out is lost. title: oneHintPer30Days counts used hint windows, not delivered hints
detail: hint() records hintLog and the reply in one step. A turn that fails after the hint keeps the window used and delivers nothing (D3). The invariant passes. The rule ('the person gets one hint') is not checked.
proposal: Split hit from collect, and add ghost hintSent (set when a gateway answer carries the hint) and an invariant that a window used in the last 30 days has a sent hint.

title: formal-main model makes the admission check and the gateway send atomic
where: claude/formal-main quint/turn_consent.qnt admitted()/answer(), service.ts sharedTurn storedTurnAdmitted
detail: In code, storedTurnAdmitted reads the ledger, then the HTTP answer returns, then the gateway sends. A STOP that commits in the compliance slot between these steps still lets an ordinary reply through until the STOP's own answer reaches the fence. The model's noReplyAfterStop cannot see this window.
proposal: Split answer() into admitted-read and deliver actions, with a STOP able to commit in between. State the remaining dependency on the fence.

title: addConsent idempotency key differs from the code
detail: The model dedupes on (ref, src). The code dedupes on (e164, ref), so a second event with the same message ref and another source is dropped. Example: a non-member START followed by join's 'inbound_message' opt-in in the same message. No current trace depends on this, but a path added later could write two events in the model where the code writes one.
proposal: Key addConsent on ref only (one sender = one e164).

title: memberUnit per-message dedupe is not modelled (reruns redo replies)
detail: A rerun (reclaim) of a member's keyword turn finds its inbound message stored and collects nothing. The model re-collects the reply on every run, so it hides D1. Adding it would break a complianceAnswered invariant for Help. STOP and leave would still pass because of turn.confirmation.
proposal: Add World.unitDone: Set[int]; memberUnit-based steps on a rerun produce no reply; add invariant complianceAnswered and run test helpRerunTest.

title: Join, START and STOP projections have commit points the model merges
detail: Join is one atomic step. In code it is putMembership(active), recordConsent, turn.consent, createMember, then stopped() or memberMessage. START sets turn.consent before updateMembership and endPause (drift open). Each gap is a crash point. Modelling them makes projectionsMatchLedger fail without the cutShort ghost (D4, drift START item).
proposal: Split the Join and Start branches into per-commit phases, and extend cutShort or replace it with a reconcile action (Q-turn_consent-4 fix).

title: Gateway retry assumption is too weak: the request hash must match
detail: digest = sha256(raw body). A retry whose bytes differ gets turn_conflict (final), and a reclaim needs the same request_hash. If a STOP's first run crashed and the gateway re-serialises or re-mints networkAuthority for its retry, the STOP is final with no ledger event. The model header assumes only 'same messageId'.
proposal: Either state 'byte-identical retries' as a gateway assumption, or add Msg.hash with a gateway action that changes it, and check stopNeverLost.

title: Recycled-number hold is fixed per run, but seen() creates it on the first message after 12 months
detail: held is a constant in the model. In code a stale number becomes held on its first non-STOP text, and activeMembership also refuses a stale phone. On HEAD this drops a held 'leave <app>' (fixed in formal-main). Modelling it would show the HEAD leave loss with leaveNeverLost and checks open-turn refusal after a long silence.
proposal: Make held' change in sendText/work when now - lastSeen > 12 months (a long tick), and keep it fixed otherwise.

title: Eliza takeover notice, onFail undo and the sweep delete are absent (plan machine eliza-takeover)
detail: The notice row commits before the join and is undone on failure, deleted by the sweep or a staff resolve, and collected as compliance. None of this is modelled. With it, the model could check 'notice at most once per number, and a failed turn returns it', and compare the notice with the stop hint (which has no undo, D3).
proposal: Add noticeRow with onFail and sweep deletes, and an invariant noticeOnceAndDelivered.

title: Claim locking: try-lock busy and the legacy drain holding the same sender key
detail: The signed claim uses pg_try_advisory_xact_lock('inbox-sender:<addr>') and answers busy on failure. The legacy drain holds the same key as a session lock for a whole handler call. So while a legacy row of the sender is handled, every signed turn, STOP included, gets turn_busy. The claim is atomic in the model, so busyKw cannot see this (extends the open drift item).
proposal: Model the lock as a resource held by the drain action and the claim; decide whether a short hold-back of a STOP is allowed, and record that decision in stopNeverHeldBack.

title: Web, MCP and enroll opt-ins and stopAt are absent
detail: There are no opt-ins without a ref at backend time, so stopAt's raise and SD-023's enroll and web halves are never exercised. A rerun of a STOP recomputes stopAt, so its echo at can differ from the stored event's at (drift open).
proposal: Add a webOptIn(app) actor (no ref, at = now) and an enroll step inside the looking_for answer.

title: Other omissions: app-scope STOP and forced-app routing, number change, open-turn binding, legacy scan limit, signals
detail: Not modelled: (1) PLATFORM_STOP_SCOPE=app with a forced app, where route returns the forced app before the SD-318 named-app START. (2) A number change during a STOP (addConsent copies the event to the new number); the model has one sender, the plan bound is 2. (3) openAllowed leaves out suppression, review, join age and stale phone from activeMembership. (4) The legacy drain scans only 50 waiting rows for a compliance row. (5) A confirmed opt_out signal changes no consent, GET /signals shows 200 rows, and the plan's signalNeverActs is absent (vacuous by construction).
proposal: Add these when the module is next extended. The first three are the most likely to change consent results.

Model: add a 'closing' phase needing no held lock connection (see model_error).

title: biasLate treats absolute time as uptime; no process restart
detail: Model process starts at 0 and never restarts, so the uptime branch of bias_late always grows; hides D3.
proposal: Add pr.startedAt reset on restart (after closed/killed) and use now - startedAt in the no-report branch; skippedWeekSeen then fails until D3 is fixed.

title: tickLateSeen is a tautology after the SD-368 fix
detail: lastSeen(tk) = tk.lastTickRan, so the invariant is p implies p; it no longer checks that an ops round raises tick_late. The no-stored-tick uptime path (ops.ts:290) is also absent.
proposal: Replace with a ghost set in opsRound: readOk and now - lastTickRan > TICK_LATE and not(cur.tick.on); add the no-stored-tick branch with uptime.

title: bootLoginComplete is vacuous
detail: member becomes true only in bootCreate, which also sets connect; init never has member without connect. checkPassedIncomplete is unreachable. Code check does not test CONNECT (harmless).
proposal: Init nondet over (member, connect) for a hand-made login, or drop the invariant and keep handMadeLoginTest as the check.

title: migrationOnce cannot fail
detail: One boot record; applied increments only when ledger is false; migrate is atomic. No two-replica boot and no crash inside the transaction, so the advisory lock is never exercised.
proposal: Per-replica boot steps with a migrate lock, or drop it from safety and note the code is one transaction under pg_advisory_xact_lock.

title: restoreRolesNotOnSource is a tautology (systemId assumed always present)
detail: onSource = internal-host or reallySource, so rolesOnSource never sets. Code compares systemId only when manifest.source.systemId exists; a manifest with source host but no systemId falls back to host strings (the SD-165 residual already listed as open drift on formal-main).
proposal: Add a nondet manifestHasSystemId; the invariant then fails for old manifests via the proxy host name; fix by refusing --roles when systemId is missing.

title: LLM 'empty' at regrow cap ends in error in the model; code returns ""
detail: Only finish_reason=length throws after MAX_REGROWS. Fixed in the formal-main model only; this branch still differs.
proposal: Split outcome into empty (ends ok) and truncated (ends error), as on formal-main.

title: skippedWeekSeen guarded by failedSinceReport; biasCheck not gated on a ran tick
detail: The rule (deploy.md 7.2, AGENTS item 12) is that a late weekly report is seen whatever the cause. Code runs weeklyBias only from afterTick after a tick that ran; the model lets biasCheck run with no tick and only checks the failure case.
proposal: Enable biasCheck only after tickRound(true) on that replica and drop the failedSinceReport conjunct from lateUnseen.

title: GRACE < KILL is a constant; code accepts SHUTDOWN_GRACE_MS >= 30000
detail: loadConfig checks only a whole number >= 0. A grace of 30 s or more makes SIGKILL win.
proposal: Make GRACE nondet in {2,3} or refuse SHUTDOWN_GRACE_MS >= drainingSeconds when deployed (config test like backend-timing-config).

title: Inbound drain and purge failures or hangs are not modelled
detail: tickRound always clears both ages. Code swallows drain/purge errors; a hung handleSender (sender advisory lock, or a unit waiting for the network lock) keeps busy('inbound') and every later round skips the inbound step. A STOP that keeps failing stays pending by design. dueHasCaller could fail.
proposal: Add nondet drain outcome (ok/fail/hang) and a stuck 'inbound' step in tickRound; expect dueHasCaller to fail on hang unless the step has a timeout.

title: In-process Queue skip: ticks starve under steady inbound load
detail: withTickLock returns undefined when this process's queue is busy; reported as 'another instance holds the lock' and stamped in tickDone (/healthz green). tick_late still fires from the stored tick, so no invariant break.
proposal: Add a queueBusy flag that makes tickRound a skip; keep tickLateSeen (rewritten) as the check.

title: afterTick SLA alerts read rt.net outside the lock (SD-448 class, only bias fixed)
detail: relayHeld() and reviewQueue() read in-memory state after runTick; a unit whose save failed in between leaves uncommitted state. Output is log lines only.
proposal: Extend biasReadsCommitted to an slaReadsCommitted ghost, or move the read into rt.readState.

title: Ops dispatcher: many networks, per-replica probe sets, stale snapshot races
detail: Every replica collects, then one wins pg_try_advisory_xact_lock. A slower replica can dispatch an older snapshot and reopen an alert just resolved; a network missing from one replica's boot-time probes is resolved by it (not in current, not unread).
proposal: Two replicas with separate snapshots in opsRound; check alertResolvedOnlyOnRead against them.

title: Restore precondition ignores an active Cloudflare container
detail: Runbook sets Railway replicas to 0; with the CF cutover active, the container keeps ticking and sending on the old database during the restore. Model requires all units idle.
proposal: Join cf.containerRunning into the restore precondition as a nondet operator step; add a runbook check.

title: Rollout overlap, restart limit and early SIGTERM not modelled
detail: Old code on the new schema during overlap; bootCrash loops forever in the model but Railway stops after 5; SIGTERM before handlers are registered (after svc.start delivers) kills at once. Safe by atomic saves and queue recovery.
proposal: Optional: bootAttempts bound and an 'old code' replica; no safety invariant expected to break.

title: LLM deadline, abort, budget and Retry-After absent; backup run (M-145) absent
detail: These only shorten the LLM loop (llmAttemptBound not at risk). The backup's ACCESS SHARE locks interact with boot migrations (SD-369).
proposal: No change needed for the LLM; model the backup snapshot only if SD-369 is taken up.

title: SD-159 inactiveStops: fixable in code, blocked by the test policy
detail: Constructor validation (BUILD_ID, config) runs on the inactive stop path, so a rollback deploy without --var BUILD_ID (or without BACKEND_RUNTIME_CONFIG, formal-main drift) cannot SIGTERM the container.
proposal: Validate only on the active path, or require BUILD_ID on rollback in the README. A test needs workerd with Containers; until then only the README rule is in scope.

title: SD-050 restoreKeepsStops (founder decision)
detail: On the blooio channel nothing outside the restored database holds an opt-out (the audit table is in the same database). Not fixable in scope without the founder choosing the record and the post-restore dry-run rule.
proposal: Keep out of safety; ask the founder for the consent record and a 'sends stay dry-run until reconciled' step.

title: SD-169 staffRouted (founder decision)
detail: Only port 8790 is routed after the CF cutover; review items expire unsent (fail closed).
proposal: No change until the founder decides the console path.

title: SD-369 not reproduced: can be reproduced now
detail: Model calls migrate atomic. The lock-queue effect (readers queued behind an ALTER waiting 60 s on pg_dump's ACCESS SHARE) stalls turns past the 8 s deadline; not measured.
proposal: Postgres integration case: RR transaction holding ACCESS SHARE, boot migrate with an ALTER, measure a concurrent query; fix with a short boot lock_timeout plus retry.

title: SD-324 skipped, but the fell_back paths are dead code
detail: Register: nothing writes 'fell_back'. Removing the unreachable smsFallback paths needs no upstream change and fits 'remove dead code'.
proposal: Remove the dead paths; no model change.

title: Findings file omits 12 in-scope register ids; other skips unchanged
detail: SD-119, SD-160, SD-234, SD-238, SD-261, SD-280, SD-305, SD-306, SD-323, SD-365, SD-449, SD-452 are in the 6.14 scope but not in section 5 (all refuted in the register). SD-096, SD-239, SD-364, SD-366, SD-371, SD-453 stay skipped (design, founder or GitHub).
proposal: Add them to section 5 as refuted with the register reason.

title: Relay rate window per sender per match (burst, daily, photos, one contact share)
detail: Per (sender, match) counters: attempts in 10 min (6) and 24 h (40) count pass/hold/block rows, passed photos in 24 h (6), delivered contact shares (1, block family). Own item id excluded (replay safe). RelayDesk.unsent rewriting a lost share to contactShared=false reopens the slot. relay.qnt:208 has 'rate' only as an oracle outcome, so no counter, no release-time asymmetry, no share-retry path. Rules: relay.ts header item 6, founder decision 9, SD-320.
proposal: Extend quint/relay.qnt: per-sender counters over the bounded log (RELAY_LOG_MAX=3); invariants atMostOneDeliveredShare(sender,match) and rateHoldOnlyFromEarlierAttempts (rate reasons count only rows with at <= item.at).

title: Peon employer probation (probation -> trusted -> back to probation)
detail: companyTrusted flips on answered>0 (or first interview) and off when the answered history row disappears (AJ20). slateCap limits an untrusted company to ceil(probationProbes/openSeats) per engine run; the documented rule is 3 probes per week until the company answers. Job seats are state 'open' with a 1000/7d budget, so nothing else bounds them. Peon matching is local only.
proposal: Extend quint/matching_engine.qnt peon part: trusted flag, probesThisWeek counter, daily engineRun action; invariant probationWeeklyCap.

title: Declared pack ConsentFlow (probe_first/double_opt_in/application/group_rsvp) is dead configuration
detail: Only the LIBRARY startProbeFlowFor reads ConsentFlow, and only kind/order. quorum, lateJoinHours, expiresHours, reveal, stages, blindReview are read by nothing; startProbeFlow hard-codes group quorum max(3, ceil(0.66n)) so event_coattend quorum 2 is never honoured. Production consent is the network Opp with PlansConfig. validatePack (core age invariants) is called only by scripts/sim/conformance.ts, not where the service builds packs.
proposal: No Quint model (no runtime state). Delete the unused fields (simplify-first), or add a sim gate that the Opp quorum/lateJoinHours/probe order equal each pack's declared ConsentFlow, and call validatePack in service/packs.ts appWiring.

title: relay.qnt: Clef classifier availability states are an oracle; degraded mode fails open for no-cue texts
detail: States: unconfigured-dev (rules only), unconfigured-prod (hook throws -> llm:error hold, fail closed), configured-up, configured-degraded (timeout/HTTP error/miss -> no flags unless RELAY_HIGH_RISK_CUE matches). With Clef configured but down, production passes no-cue texts on rules alone (~50-60% on unseen phrasing per AGENTS.md). The cue regex tests raw text while the rules use textVariants, so obfuscated asks the rules miss also miss the cue. The model has no env/availability variable, so 'a passed prod text was read by Clef or had no cue' cannot be stated.
proposal: Extend quint/relay.qnt with clefEnv in {off, prodClosed, live}, clefUp: bool, ghost passedUnread, and a named non-safety value prodNoUnreadPass pending a founder decision on degraded mode.

title: photos_rating.qnt: the Clef photo rater call cannot hang in the model
detail: WorkersAIClefRater.ask calls clefRun with no AbortSignal and ClefRaterOptions has no timeout (the relay hook has a 2.5 s race). withRetry retries TimeoutError/AbortError, which nothing raises. The model's rater returns a score, null or an error only.
proposal: Add a 'hang' outcome and a stalled in-flight rating to quint/photos_rating.qnt, with a liveness witness that an upload answers.

title: plan_run.qnt leaves out partner plans, which are wired in production
detail: The planner makes partner plans of 2 (partnerPlans: true) when no group clears; beginPlan/startPlanRun probes only invited[0]; first yes -> probe_partner before the deadline; first no closes; partner no backfills the next alternate. plan_run.qnt says partner plans are not modelled (reasoning from SD-008/partnerPlanFor), but the planner's own partner plans run through the same path. Core invariant 6 (consent before reveal) and the one-to-one order have no model.
proposal: Extend quint/plan_run.qnt: partner flag on the plan, sequential first/partner stage; invariants partnerNotBeforeFirstYes, firstNoCloses; witness a partner plan books.

title: matching_engine.qnt: slop extra-asks ladder partial (orientation/age_range/distance, widen, type)
detail: Model has the basics ask and the location ask only. Missing: weekly hard-field asks capped by maxAsksPerField (with silentFallback off a capped field leaves the member in needs_answer for good, by design), the once-ever widen ask whose plain 'yes' sets radius 25 mi via classifyYesNo with no read-back, and the 21-day type ask. Complements the formal-main open drift (per-question caps, soft questions).
proposal: Add per-field hardAsk counters, widenAsked, and invariant widenOnlyRaisesRadiusOnYes to quint/matching_engine.qnt.

title: matching_engine.qnt probe-flow: group/quorum branch and answer flips not modelled (LIBRARY)
detail: flowStart takes 1 or 2 participants; group quorum reveal/close and reveal-only-to-yes are absent. recordProbeAnswer accepts a second answer from a member while the stage is open (no pending guard), so a yes can flip to no and close a group. No production caller today.
proposal: Model when wired (section 6.18 rule): add n=3 groups with quorum to the flow part of quint/matching_engine.qnt.

title: slop-assignment (M-162) and attention-compose (M-163) mapped to matching_engine but absent
detail: Assignment rounds and stable roommates are one nondeterministic engine pick; composeMessage gate order (wired only on the plan allowance path) is a deferral oracle in plan_run. LemmaScript cores on formal-main cover the arithmetic; the formal-coverage ledger text overstates Quint coverage.
proposal: Keep both as oracles; correct the ledger rows for assign.ts and attention.ts to say 'oracle in matching_engine/plan_run'.

detail: The model has the rating row and the Clef oracle. It does not model the transitions 'weights changed', 'ratings switched off' or 're-rate', so it cannot show the defect above.
proposal: Add weights:int and ratingsOn:bool, and a version on each rating row. New invariants ratingsMatchWeights and offMeansUnused: both fail on the current code.

title: The slop widen ask (one-shot radius widening) is in no model
detail: States: not_eligible -> asked -> widened (yes) | kept (no, other text, silence). The ask goes once, when the run degree is <=2 and the limit is under 25 miles. runDegree is a WeakMap that the generator writes and extraAsks reads in the same World. A yes with no new distance sets radius 25. sendAsks sends the onboarding loop's question instead while the loop has one left. A grep for 'widen' in quint/ finds nothing.
proposal: Add this to the matching_engine per-question ask-count change that the drift review already requires (nextMsg, basicsAskDue). Invariants: widenAskedOnce, and widenOnlyOnYes (the radius grows only when classifyYesNo returns yes).

title: attention-compose (M-163) on the wired plan-allowance path is not modelled
detail: The catalog assigns M-163 to matching_engine, but that model's header and actions have no compose, ledger, cap or streak state. plan_run treats the allowance as a nondeterministic deferral. So nothing checks 'at most 1 allowance plan invite per 7 days' or 'no allowance invite while two are unanswered'. reviewState is hard-coded 'approved' on this path.
proposal: Extend plan_run: add planInvites: str->List[int] and the cap and two-unanswered gates as guards on planProbe. Invariant allowanceCap.

title: notify_capital Part B has no debit, stake or stewardship events, but production emits them
detail: The model's actions are cJoin, cActivate, cLearnMinor, cPlanAccept, cSayGood, cFinalize, cHelp, cForget and cRestart. Its header says the rest have 'no production trigger'. That is true only for the fraud flags. plan_confirmed, plan_cancelled, plan_no_show, plan_ghosted, safety_flag, abuse_confirmed, member_removed (stake and vouch reversal), organized, need_answered and review_completed are all emitted and stored in network.capital_events, and replay must reproduce them. The effect is latent today (runtime.ts:121 reader:false).
proposal: Add plan states {accepted, confirmed, resolved} and the actions cConfirm, cCancel, cNoShow, cGhost, cFlag and cRemoveAbuse. Invariants: debitNeedsCommitment, stakeOnce, clawbackOnce, and ineligibleNeverDebited (holds on the code). Extend replayEqualsLive to the debit events.

title: Judge passes 1 and 3 caches are not modelled, and stale cache keys are never evicted
detail: The code has three TTL caches (screen, judge, deep); matching_engine models one. A key whose participant revision changed is never read again, so JudgeCache never deletes it. The map grows for the process lifetime, by about topK entries per run per app. Passes 1 and 3 are off by default, so the effect is latent.
proposal: No Quint change for now. Record the abstraction in the matching_engine header. If passes 1 or 3 are turned on, add their cache keys to the judgeCacheReused witness.

title: Peon employer probation -> trusted (derived per company) is not modelled
detail: States: probation or trusted. A company becomes trusted after an answered application, and goes back to probation when that application leaves the history window. Probation caps the slate at 3 probes, or 10 for an urgent verified role, split across the company's open seats. Only code comments state the rules. Peon matching is local only.
proposal: Extend the matching_engine peon part with trusted: bool and slate cap 1 vs 2. Low value: no safety rule depends on it.

title: Engine judge LLM budget: one process-wide budget that stays exhausted until restart
detail: States: open(spent, requests), then exhausted, which lasts until the process restarts (a restart resets the budget). take() runs before each attempt and charge() after the response. The request limit is exact. The dollar limit can be passed by in-flight calls (concurrency 4 per app, and all apps share one budget). Once exhausted, judge calls fail at once, failures are not cached, and pass 2 fails open to unjudged proposals. Hard filters still run first, so there is no safety effect.
proposal: Do not model it in Quint. If a bound is wanted, add an integration case for the dollar overshoot.

title: A planned engine ask takes a proposal slot that the Network may never use

title: A Cloud fence opt-out never reaches the backend ledger or member projection
detail: When Cloud answers a deliver with opted_out, the row ends 'blocked' and onAlert writes only a log line. The ledger and network.members.opted_out are not changed. turn_consent feeds the fence only from the backend's echo, in one direction. No model has a state where the fence is opted out and the ledger is opted in. Trigger: the fence holds an older STOP (from a web join with no echo, the SD-023 half; from a recycled number after a new_owner decision, which deletes the old owner's ledger rows but leaves the fence row; or from a STOP the gateway answered itself after turn_unresolved). The ledger resolves opted_in. The tick selects the member, a reviewer approves, and the queue admits the row. Cloud answers opted_out and the row ends blocked. The Network still believes the probe went out (SD-006 family), and the counterpart waits until the item expires. This repeats on every cycle.
proposal: Extend turn_consent with the actions fenceOptOut(app) and deliverRefused(app), and add a knownOpen invariant noMatchAgainstFence. A possible code fix folds a blocked/opted_out row into the ledger (source cloud_fence) or pauses the member. This needs a founder decision, because only STOP and leave may change consent.

title: Cloud-side per-phone state (fence, Eliza history) is outside every identity saga
detail: The wire contract has no erase, ban, number-move or new-owner message. Accepted deliveries and turn replies carry historyRecorded/history true, so Eliza Cloud keeps Network replies, proactive texts and relayed texts in its history per phone. deleteAll, ban, new_owner and movePhone change only the backend. States per phone on the Cloud side: none, history, history+fence_out. Trigger: B relays a text to A, and Cloud delivers it with history. B deletes everything (or staff do it after an e-mail, SD-255). B's relayed words stay in A's Eliza history, and B's Network conversation stays in B's. Add the invariant eraseReachesCloud in knownOpen until upstream adds an erase message. The contract change lands upstream first (founder and upstream decision).

title: START writes ledger and echo before the membership resumes; a turn that is not retried leaves the membership paused
detail: The code order is: recordConsent(opted_in), turn.consent=opted_in, updateMembership(paused->active), endPause. If a throw comes after the ledger write, the turn fails. The membership resumes only if the gateway retries the same message, because the retry then finds optedIn true. If the retries run out, the ledger says opted in and the membership stays paused, with no notice to the member. The formal-main drift review lists this as open; I confirmed the order on this branch.
proposal: Split START in turn_consent into startLedger and startMembership with a crash point between them. Add the quiescence invariant startResumesMembership.

detail: The model has one rate slot. Two uploads start two rate() runs. Scores are never shown, so no safety rule breaks, but matching uses a stale score until the next upload or delete.

title: Rate window store (platform.rate_limits: hit/hitAll/purge with keep_until)
detail: States per bucket are fixed-window rows (window_start, count, last_at, keep_until), with at most 2 windows kept. Transitions: a counted hit, a refused hit (no write), all-or-none hitAll in bucket-name lock order, and the purge at now-2d that keeps rows until keep_until. Rules: a refused hit never counts; hitAll counts in all buckets or in none; a minGap row survives the purge; every bucket with a window longer than the purge age has a minGap at least that long (today only stop_hint, which complies). Note: with fixed windows, '3 per hour' allows 5 sends in about 2 minutes across an hour edge (the day limit 6 still holds). The memory store and the Pg store agree. Only turn_consent (stop_hint, M-007) and auth_edge (the abstract OTP start buckets) touch this store.
proposal: Low Quint value: each call is one transaction with nothing to interleave. Recommend a static rule in runtime_ops (retention, M-140): window > purge age implies minGap >= window, checked over the bucket table, plus formal-main's verified hitPasses core. Put the verify buckets in auth_edge (see the auth_edge gap).

title: Cloud validation TTL cache (validated map) in the public API
detail: An in-memory Map<sessionHash, until>, absent or valid-until(t). It is set on the callback, on rotation (without revalidation) and on a positive validate. It is deleted on a bad identity cookie or a denial, and cleared above 10000 entries. Rule: a denial is never cached. Production Cloud mode bypasses it (api.ts:273), so it runs only for the staging/local tuple.
proposal: Extend auth_edge (M-060 cloud-session-validation) only if the staging Cloud mode remains. Value is low because there is no production path.

title: Share offer and share grant (pending kind 'share' plus platform.share_grants)
detail: The pending share row (purged after 2 days) becomes grants on a SHARE answer, one for each other live membership. A grant goes from granted to revoked (revokeShare, forgetMembership), and deleteAll deletes the row. Rules: only shareable fields, and both memberships live. title: stoppedIsHonest does not check that a final code stops the loop
detail: The comment says a final LLMError (aborted, deadline, budget) ends the loop at once, but the invariant only checks r.attempts <= started. Mutant m1 sets `val final = false`, so final codes are retried, and it passes `quint run --invariant=safety` (12 steps, 6000 samples). Only the fixed trace clientDeadlineStopsTest catches it. Report: scratchpad/wave3/audit-chatjson_loop.md.

title: No invariant says no call starts after the caller signal aborts
detail: Mutant m7 makes attemptGate ignore `aborted` and uses DEADLINE_CHOICES = {0}. It passes safety. Mutant m2 (the same change, with all deadline choices) is caught only through deadlineStopsLoop. Only the abortTest run checks the cancellation rule (chatJson.ts:26-27, llm.ts:26).
proposal: Add a ghost startedAfterAbort, set when loopPass starts a call while aborted, and the invariant not(startedAfterAbort) in safety.

title: callTimeBounded cannot fail: it restates the step assumption
detail: Without a loop deadline, callDl = CLIENT_DL and the step requires d <= callDl, so callTime <= started*CLIENT_DL holds by construction. No mutation of a code-mapped decision can break it. The bound actually comes from llm.ts:278-298, which is not in the model.
proposal: Model the client deadline as an input that can be missing (see the CLIENT_DL item), or mark the invariant as an assumption and not a checked rule.

title: The model assumes every LLM honours ChatOptions.deadlineMs and signal
detail: `d <= callDl` is what makes deadlineStopsLoop's callEndMax <= deadlineAt hold. LLM is an interface. Only OpenAILLM enforces deadlineMs and signal. Other implementations (scripts/sim/conformance.ts:40, test doubles, engine appearance clients) can ignore them. The invariant describes the OpenAILLM client, not tryChatJson.
proposal: Add a nondet honours: bool per call. When it is false, let d go past callDl and make the end-time half of deadlineStopsLoop conditional on it, or write the assumption explicitly in the header and the invariant name.

title: CLIENT_DL > 0 hides the unbounded call when LLM_TIMEOUT_MS=0
detail: LLM_TIMEOUT_MS=0 makes the default deadline 3x0 = 0, which means no deadline (core.md D9). A hung request then never ends, and a loop without deadlineMs waits forever. The model fixes CLIENT_DL=3, so the only unbounded configuration is outside the model.
proposal: Add a CLIENT_DL 'none' choice and a witness for unbounded callTime. In code (in scope as an ops/security fix), refuse LLM_TIMEOUT_MS=0 unless LLM_DEADLINE_MS > 0 is set.

title: okOnlyAfterValidation is close to a tautology; validated is still a literal
detail: Ok is built with validated: true in the same branch that tests code == 'valid' and sets lastOutcome' = code. Mutant m6 (invalid treated as valid) is caught, but the invariant only has force against that one branch condition. parse is an oracle.
proposal: Keep it, but derive validated from a separate parse oracle (parseOk nondet) so that the value and the outcome are independent inputs.

title: One clock in the model; the shell and the client use two
detail: The loop deadline uses o.clock. The client computes its own deadline from hooks.clock ?? realClock and adds `left` at a later instant (after the llm(attempt) factory runs). With a SimClock in ChatJsonOptions and a real client, the two units differ. Even with one clock, the real end time is t(llm.ts:247)+left, which is after deadlineAt. The header covers only the AbortSignal.timeout rounding. No caller sets clock today.
proposal: State in the header that the shell clock and the client clock are assumed to be the same, and that the factory time is zero. Or model a nondet gap between the gate read and the call start.

title: The never-throws rule for afterAttempt and grow has no action or invariant
detail: tryChatJson promises that a paid, valid reply is never discarded, even when afterAttempt or grow throws. No check fails if either try/catch is removed. grown is a counter with no invariant, so moving grow (after a stop, or not at all) also passes. Adding these cannot break the current invariants.
proposal: Add a nondet callbackThrows to loopPass, and the invariant 'a valid outcome gives Ok' (the loop never ends with Fail after a valid outcome). Optionally add grown == number of non-final failures.

title: The factory llm(attempt) and an LLMError thrown by parse are not modeled

title: The request and budget bound per loop is not composed with runtime_ops

detail: The model covers production only (no cache). In staging and dev, validated: Map<sessionHash, until> has a 60 s TTL. Trace: request A's validate() is in flight. Cloud revokes the session.
